findings.title: hub4j signals a 404 with FileNotFoundException (IOException), so missing config files land in the READ_FAILED branch and the negative cache is never written
findings.description: The migration keeps the 404/absent distinction on the wrong exception type. The RuntimeException catch now guards the absent case with `if (e instanceof jakarta.ws.rs.NotFoundException)`, but the Quarkiverse GitHub App extension hands you a hub4j `GHRepository`, whose `getFileContent(path, ref)` declares `throws IOException` and signals a missing file with a `FileNotFoundException` subclass (`GHFileNotFoundException`) — it never throws a Jakarta REST exception. So a genuine 404 for `.github/thrillhousebot.yml` falls into `catch (IOException e)` at line 197, which returns `Fetched.READ_FAILED`: the resolver warns on every review (once per candidate path) and, because `READ_FAILED` results are deliberately not cached (the fail-soft rule the tests describe as "a failure we cannot read is not an answer to cache"), the negative cache is never written for repos without a config file. That recreates exactly the behavior the file's own history documents as a bug (##481: "treating them as a 404 pinned 'this repo has no config'" was the OLD wrong direction; the new structure re-loses "a real 404 is a real answer and is cached"). Please verify against the hub4j version resolved by `quarkus-github-app` that `getFileContent` throws `GHFileNotFoundException` on 404; if so, catch it explicitly as an absent answer. The tests keep passing only because `stubMissing` stubs the impossible exception type (see the separate mock finding on RepoSettingsResolverTest).

findings.title: InstructionsResolver caches a null-content file and then swallows its own NPE, so later resolves return null instructions from the cache
Tests stub jakarta.ws.rs.NotFoundException from GHRepository.getFileContent — an exception the real hub4j method cannot throw
findings.description:
`stubMissing` now reads:

    doThrow(new jakarta.ws.rs.NotFoundException())
        .when(repository)
        .getFileContent(path, DEFAULT_BRANCH);

and `theClientsOwn404IsNoConfigAndIsCachedLikeOne` stubs the same exception on every path. The real collaborator is hub4j's `GHRepository`, whose `getFileContent(String, String)` declares `throws IOException` and reports a missing file with a `FileNotFoundException` subclass; it never raises `jakarta.ws.rs.NotFoundException`. Because the stub throws an unchecked exception, the tests compile and pass — but they no longer test the production 404 path at all: `aRealNotFoundIsStillCachedAsNoConfig` ("the client's 404 is a real answer and is cached") verifies a code path that only exists for an exception hub4j never emits, which is why the corresponding regression in the catch structure of `RepoSettingsResolver.fetchAndParse` is invisible to the suite. Please confirm the hub4j behavior with the resolved `github-api` version (404 ⇒ `GHFileNotFoundException`, a checked `IOException`) and stub that type instead.

findings.title: cachesAreKeyedPerRepository had its expected value changed to match a stub override, and now verifies nothing
Caching tests across this migration dropped their fetch-count assertions, so TTL expiry and refetch regressions now pass silently
findings.description: The old tests pinned the fetch counts that prove caching works; the migration deleted them without replacement. In `cachesPerRepositoryAndRefetchesAfterTheTtl` the pair `verify(prClient, times(1)).getFileContent(...)` / `verify(prClient, times(2)).getFileContent(...)` around the TTL advance is gone, so a resolver that never caches (or never expires) still passes — both resolves return the same value. The same happened in `negativeResultIsCachedBrieflyThenRetried` (the post-TTL `resolve` result isn't even assigned or asserted anymore), `aReadableButUnusableConfigIsCachedLikeAnyOtherAnswer` (now just the comment "// configured file was the only one read"), `aReadableButUnusableConfigIsHeldForTheFullTtlNotTheNegativeOne`, `theClientsOwn404IsNoConfigAndIsCachedLikeOne`, and in ProjectStackResolverTest's `shouldCacheStackAndNotHitApiOnSecondCall` and `productionConstructorShouldResolveWithSystemClock`. The negative-cache TTLs (CACHE_TTL_MS, NEGATIVE_CACHE_TTL_MS) are exactly the behavior class this PR's history shows has regressed before, so they should keep a count-based assertion — e.g. `verify(repository, times(2)).getFileContent(anyString(), anyString())` after the TTL advance.

findings.title: A git merge-conflict marker was committed into the security model document
findings.description:
The added text contains a diff3-style conflict label as real document content:

    Organization membership is granted only on GitHub's explicit answer. Optional context and outgoing
    ||||||| parent of 602b19b (refactor(webhook): adopt Quarkiverse GitHub App extension for webhook entry)
    `WebhookEvents` runs behind the Quarkiverse GitHub App extension's route, which rejects a
    request when the signature header is missing or when no secret is configured. The dashboard refuses every login
    when the App owner cannot be resolved. Optional context and outgoing
    notifications are off until enabled, and a manual `/review` needs write access

The `||||||| parent of 602b19b (...)` line is unresolved-conflict residue, and the paragraph is left garbled with "Optional context and outgoing" duplicated on both sides of it. The intended merged sentence appears to be: extension route rejects a request when the signature header is missing or no secret is configured, dashboard refuses every login when the App owner cannot be resolved, then "Optional context and outgoing notifications are off until enabled...".

findings.title: Each candidate path now re-issues the repository lookup — repeated GitHub API round trips per resolve where one would do
Feature-disabled check verifies the same mock twice; the migrated authClient assertion has no replacement
Webhook-entry changelog bullet duplicated verbatim under a re-opened '### Changed' heading
findings.description:
The diff adds a new `### Changed` heading immediately followed by a bullet that repeats, word for word, the already-present entry at the end of the previous section:

    - The webhook entry now rides the Quarkiverse GitHub App extension (`io.quarkiverse.githubapp:quarkus-github-app`): it owns the `POST /api/webhook` route, the `X-Hub-Signature-256` check and delivery parsing, and `webhook/WebhookEvents` keeps the existing routing (dedupe, pause, trigger filters, commands, CI rechecks). `WebhookController` and `WebhookVerifier` are gone. Malformed-request answers change to the extension's (`400` for missing/mismatched signature, `500` for a signed non-JSON body, `200` with an empty body on success).

That text appears twice in the release notes now, and the extra `### Changed` heading is redundant under the section that already contains it. Drop the heading and the duplicated bullet and keep only the three new migration bullets.
